title: Steamed Asparagus with Lemon-Tarragon Almond Cream
description: Short asparagus pieces stay crisp-tender under a smooth tarragon sauce enriched with blanched almond paste.

ingredients.name: trimmed fresh asparagus
ingredients.note: Cut off woody ends, peel thick bases and cut stalks into 1-inch pieces, keeping tips separate.

ingredients.name: smooth unsalted blanched almond paste
ingredients.note: Pure ground blanched almonds without sugar.

steps.title: Make the almond cream
steps.text: Whisk {almond}, {broth} and {tarragon} in a small saucepan over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes until smooth and thick enough to ribbon from the whisk.

steps.title: Steam the stems
steps.text: Bring {water} to a simmer in the HexClad skillet. Add the stem pieces of {asparagus}, cover, and steam for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Add the tips
steps.text: Add the reserved tips, cover again, and steam for 1–3 minutes until crisp-tender and bright green.

steps.title: Perfume the sauce
steps.text: Take the almond cream off the heat and fold in {zest}.

steps.title: Dress the asparagus
steps.text: Lift the pieces out with a slotted spoon and spoon warm almond cream generously over both portions.

notes: Make ahead: Make the almond cream a day ahead, chilling it separately. Steam the asparagus close to serving time. Refrigerate in shallow portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. Frozen asparagus softens substantially, though the almond sauce alone freezes well for a month. Fridge reheat: Heat covered in the skillet with a splash of water for 3–5 minutes until the vegetables and sauce reach 165°F. Freezer reheat: Thaw in the refrigerator overnight, then follow the fridge reheat instructions. Option A uses lemon zest for fragrance. Option B leaves it out and adds a little more tarragon for a gentler finish. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 96 kcal, 5.5 g protein, 6.8 g total carbohydrate, 6.4 g fat, 3.6 g fiber, 12 mg sodium.
